title: Jalapeño Popper Pizza
subtitle: Cream cheese, bacon, pickled heat
description: Cream cheese, bacon, pickled heat. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Whip popper spread
steps.instruction: Beat cream cheese with sour cream, garlic powder, and salt until smooth. Fold in half the bacon. This replaces tomato sauce — keep it spreadable, not chunky.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 475°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 475°F at least 35 minutes. Cream cheese pies scorch above 500°F on the bottom before the center sets.

steps.title: Stretch rounds and spread base
steps.instruction: Stretch dough to 12–14 inches. Spread a thin layer of popper cream cheese mix edge to edge, leaving a rim. Too thick and the center stays cool.

steps.title: Cheese, jalapeños, bacon
steps.instruction: Layer mozzarella and cheddar, pickled jalapeños, fresh jalapeños if using, and remaining bacon. Press jalapeños into cheese so they do not roll off on the peel.

steps.title: Bake until cheddar bubbles
steps.instruction: Bake 11–14 minutes until cheddar edges brown and the crust is crisp underneath. Jalapeño Popper Pizza should taste like the appetizer — if it tastes like plain cheese bread, add more jalapeños next time.

steps.title: Rest and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes — cream cheese stays molten. Cut 8 slices per pie. Warn the crew about fresh jalapeño heat; keep ranch nearby for rookies.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Jalapeño Popper Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cream cheese, bacon, pickled heat. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free pizza crust.
